title: In-Situ High-Temperature X-Ray Diffraction Study of Phase Transformation in MOCVD-Grown GeO2 Thin Films: Amorphous to Quartz and Rutile
content: Rutile germanium oxide (r-GeO2) has emerged as a promising ultra-wide bandgap (UWBG) semiconductor, offering a bandgap of 4.68 eV, ambipolar dopability, and a high Baliga Figure of Merit (BFOM) [1-3]. Among its two polymorphs, rutile and quartz, the rutile phase is the most thermodynamically stable [4], while quartz GeO2 is water-soluble [5], and it may pose significant challenges in device fabrication. Understanding how high-temperature annealing influences the phase stability and transformation of GeO2 is crucial for its practical application. Identifying the structural properties of GeO2 using X-ray diffraction has a critical impact on improving its properties and maximizing its application [6]. In this study, we utilize in-situ high-temperature X-ray diffraction (XRD) to examine the phase transitions of amorphous GeO2 films to quartz and rutile phases under controlled annealing conditions, conducted in two different environments: air and vacuum (at a pressure of 5 × 10-3 mbar).
